provisions.summary: Adds a new 10.25 per cent TAT rate (one point above the 9.25 per cent rate) for transient accommodations from January 1, 2026, and for resort time share vacation units; the bill's description says it raises TAT rates by 1 percentage point, with the extra revenue going to the Hawaiian home general loan fund.
provisions.approximation: The bill's text is hard to read as a clean change. Its rate ladder moves from 9.25 per cent to 10.25 per cent on January 1, 2026, and it also keeps the existing one-point increase in subsection (e) (through December 31, 2030) while rewriting it to apply to the rates in subsections (a) and (c). If the model's current TAT rate already counts the 10.25 per cent in force (9.25 plus the 1 point from subsection (e)), the bill adds a further 1 point on top, which is what the description says and what is modeled. If the reviewer reads it instead as merely restating existing law, the estimate is too high (the true change would be zero). Confirm against the model's baseline rate.
provisions.quote: (6) 10.25 per cent for the period beginning on January 1, 2026, and thereafter;

provisions.summary: Directs the revenue above what the 9.25 per cent rate would have yielded (the new one-point increase) into the Hawaiian home general loan fund; the revenue allocation does not change the estimate.
provisions.quote: shall be deposited quarterly into the Hawaiian home general loan fund established pursuant to section 213

provisions.summary: Provides that moneys received under HRS 237D-2(f) go into the Hawaiian home general loan fund; this is an allocation of revenue with no effect on the estimate.
provisions.quote: moneys received pursuant to section 237D-2(f), Hawaii Revised Statutes;

provisions.summary: Excludes the section 237D-2(f) revenues from the priority distribution under section 237D-6.5(b), so they do not feed the Turtle Bay, convention center, tourism emergency or special land funds; a change in how revenue is divided.
provisions.quote: Except for the revenues collected pursuant to section 237D-2(e)[,] and (f)

notes: Effective date: the bill takes effect upon approval (Section 6), so effective is null. The rate change is written as beginning January 1, 2026, a date already past as of this draft's evaluation (today is 2026-11-27), so a reviewer should decide how much of tax year 2026 to count; the bill has no later start date to use. Revenue allocation: the extra one point goes to the Hawaiian home general loan fund, which does not change the estimate. The existing subsection (e) one-point increase (to the mass transit special fund, through December 31, 2030) is kept; the bill lists the post-2025 rate as 10.25 per cent in subsection (a)(6) and (c)(4) and the existing (e) increase sits on top of those, so the description's statement that the rate rises by 1 percentage point is the reading modeled. Check that the baseline already includes the 2026 step to 10.25 per cent and the subsection (e) point, since the draft rewrites both.
